reviews.body: Logic is fine, but the handler is doing the service's job. See inline.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: This is the pattern ADR-003 is meant to stop: the handler opens the session, runs the charge lookup and passes the session into the service. Please move the lookup and the session into `refund_service.create_refund(charge_id=..., amount=..., reason=...)` and have the handler just call it. Missing charge should be `errors.NotFound` from the service; the handler shouldn't need `charge_repo` at all.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: I passed the session in so the lookup, the insert and the `refunded_amount` update share one transaction. But the service can do all three inside its own `session_scope()`, so there's no reason for the handler to own it. Moving it.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Done. Handler is now four lines; the service owns the session and raises NotFound.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: Perfect, that's the shape I want the rest of the handlers to end up in.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: Add a docstring to `_refundable`, e.g. whether it accounts for pending refunds. Future readers won't know.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Same answer as on #102: private helpers are documented by their names, and we only write docstrings for the public service functions. It's one subtraction; if the semantics change (say pending refunds get excluded) the name and the tests change with it.

threads.rejection_reason: Private helpers are documented by their names; we only document public service functions.
